criterion: HW H1.1: inline ray query (DXR 1.1 RayQuery) closest hits against the CPU BVH (mission-control 2026-10-10-engine-hw/PLAN.md)
written: 2026-10-10, before the implementation and the first run
reference: raw/renderer/bvh.hpp Bvh::closest (M3, read only): binned SAH, two-sided Moeller-Trumbore with |det| < 1e-7 rejected as parallel, hits with t > 1e-4, ties to the lower triangle index
gpu: one bottom-level structure of all triangles (opaque, no index buffer), one instance, a cs_6_5 kernel with RayQuery<RAY_FLAG_FORCE_OPAQUE>, TMin 1e-4, no culling; it writes t, the committed barycentrics and the committed primitive index
scenes: procedural, generated by our code (src/tools/hw_scenes.cpp), coordinates within [-10, 10]: terrain (a 160 x 160 heightfield, 51,200 triangles with shared edges), hall (floor, walls, 24 columns of 32 sides, a stair, about 10,000 triangles), debris (30,000 random triangles of edge 0.02 to 0.2 in a 4-unit cube, overlapping and crossing)
rays: per scene, three kinds: camera (a 400 x 400 pinhole grid, 160,000 rays), random (origins in the bounds, uniform directions, 100,000), ambient occlusion (origins on random surface points offset 1e-3 along the normal, cosine directions, tMax 2, 80,000). 340,000 rays a scene, 1,020,000 in all; tMax 1e30 except AO.

definitions.L: the largest absolute coordinate of the ray origin and the vertices of the triangles involved
definitions.h: the smallest altitude of the triangle involved

agreeing_hits.what: rays where both sides hit the same triangle
agreeing_hits.bound: |t_gpu - t_cpu| <= t_tol and |u_gpu - u_cpu|, |v_gpu - v_cpu| <= uv_tol on every such ray

disagreements.what: rays where the triangle differs or one side misses. Each is explained when at least one holds: edge (the hitting side's min(u, v, 1 - u - v) <= uv_tol); tie (both hit and |t_gpu - t_cpu| <= t_tol); grazing (the CPU's |det| for the GPU's triangle is below 1e-6, ten times its parallel threshold); boundary (a hit t within t_tol of TMin or tMax)
disagreements.bound: unexplained disagreements: 0; explained disagreements: at most 1e-3 of the rays of each scene

control_offset.bound: unexplained disagreements or agreeing-hit violations above 0 on every scene

control_rotate.what: every GPU ray direction rotated by 1 degree about a fixed axis; the CPU keeps the original rays
control_rotate.bound: unexplained disagreements above 0 on every scene

fallback.bound: the tool takes the CPU traversal fallback and reports it; agreement exact (it is the reference)

timing: reported, not bounded, in this slice: GPU timestamps around the trace dispatch, 50 warm-up and 500 measured repeats per scene and ray kind on the RTX 4090 (5 on WARP, recorded for completeness only); median, p5, p95, p99 and IQR, and rays per second at the median. No speedup is claimed here: the compute baseline is RT's compute BVH traversal, which has not landed; the comparison is a later step with its own bounds.
adapters: D3D12 WARP (debug layer) locally and in CI; the RTX 4090 only under D:/gpu.lock.d
does_not_prove: Any speedup; correctness of any-hit, alpha testing, instancing with real transforms, or ray tracing pipelines; that edge and tie disagreements are harmless for every renderer that will use them.
